assign.request: Search the framework for a tree UI component. We want a tree UI component to be the basis of the page interaction drag and drop. So compare those if they're two separate ones and we want to merge that together so that we can render a tree of navigation links. But they should be expandable and collapsible. Maybe the tree should adapt so that as you drill down in the tree, each selection changes the visibility in terms of siblings and how deep and whatnot. Getting that right, I think, is going to take a little practice.
assign.now: comparing the three trees that exist
steps: Compare the three trees (ux/Tree, ui/tree, Make) and the two near-trees (core/Sidebar, demo.tree)
Merge Make's edge-model drag into ux/Tree behind one move() event
Row affordances: default star, optional + and x
Tree.from(page) - navigation links from a Page subtree
The module page: one screen, live tree first, five-level draggable demo
Headless proof: three drag shots, the fold, adapt at depth 4, row count vs page count

log.msg: COMPARISON. Three trees exist, and only one is a reusable component. (1) ux/Tree (Tree.js 147 + TreeKeys.js 126 + TreeDrag.js 159): rows from a plain nodes array, expand/collapse by chevron, keyboard ONLY in TreeKeys, drag ONLY in TreeDrag, selection on the tree, no lines, no marks, no acts. (2) ui/tree (tree.js 40): CSS + hand-written static markup only - the .ui-tree-* template the class wears; no behavior at all since the 2026-08-21 graduation. (3) /imagine/paging/make/tree.js (343): rows from a page tree, NO expand/collapse (every level always open), no keyboard, drag by grip with the EDGE model (above/inside/below), selection by pick, a default star, + and x acts, writes through made.js. Two near-trees: core/Sidebar is a FLAT list with one level of grouping (no nesting, no expand, no drag); demo.tree() is not a tree widget at all - it is a demo page shape wrapping a whole mini APP.

THE DEFECT THE MERGE FIXES, measured by reading: ux/Tree ships keyboard and drag as SIBLING subclasses (TreeKeys extends Tree, TreeDrag extends Tree), so no consumer can have both. Make needed both and built its own tree instead - which is why three trees exist. DECISION: the merged tree lives in ux/Tree as ONE class; keyboard becomes part of the base (a roving tabindex is one tab stop, not thirty), drag/adapt/acts are opt-in flags, and TreeKeys.js + TreeDrag.js stay as back-compat shims so the documented API keeps working. ui/tree stays the markup it wears. Make's tree becomes a consumer in a LATER task (it is read-only in this brief).

ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED - Make's tree as the base. Caveat that rules it out: Make's tree is welded to Make. Its rows carry a PATH into made.js, its drop commits through page.move_to(), it has no expand/collapse at all (every level renders open, which is why a deep page tree is a wall), and it lives in /imagine/ where nothing else can import it. Taking it as the base would mean deleting its writer half and re-adding folding - more work than lifting its ONE good idea, the edge model, into ux/Tree.

PROPOSAL (not an edit, both are outside this fence): core/Sidebar should NOT consume the merged tree - it is a flat link list with a group heading, and a tree would add nesting nothing asks for. Make's tree SHOULD consume it: it would delete ~200 of its 343 lines (TreeItem, TreeSort, locate/up/after, node_row) and gain folding and the keyboard it has never had; what stays is its three acts wired to act(name, node) and its move handler wired to move({node, into, index}). demo.tree() is unrelated - a demo page shape, not a widget.

ext/JSONL check: TaskJSONL.verbs already lists decision and verdict and declares decisions = [] / verdicts = [], but there is NO decision() or verdict() method - JSONL.apply() calls this[verb](value), so a decision line would throw TypeError and take the whole log render down. Using log lines instead, as the brief allows. The sibling adding the verb tonight needs the two handler methods.

assign.now: merged class built and proven headless; writing the docs

log.msg: DRAG PROVEN, three targets, zero console errors (drive.mjs, 1280x1000, /framework/ux/Tree/). ABOVE: grip of Jackets to the TOP edge of Shoes (y = row.top + 4 of a 10px band) fired move({ node: Jackets, into: Men, index: 0 }) and the rows read Shop, Men, Jackets, Shoes. INSIDE: the same grip to the MIDDLE of Shoes fired move({ node: Jackets, into: Shoes, index: 2 }) and Jackets left the visible list because Shoes is shut. BELOW: grip of Kids to the BOTTOM edge of Men fired move({ node: Kids, into: Shop, index: 1 }) and the rows read Shop, Men, Shoes, Jackets, Kids, Women. The cue is right in each: an outline on the row for into, a 2px line before or after the whole li for beside.

ADAPT MEASURED at depth 4: 138 rows visible with every branch open, 12 with adapt on and a depth-4 row selected - the three roots, the three children of the one on the path, its two, its two, and the selected row's own two. Readout on the page says the same: '12 of 138 rows visible'. Fold proven in the same run: 8 rows on arrival, 138 after 'Open every branch', 12 after 'Adapt'. Depth-4 selection path read back as 'Shop / Men / Shoes / Running'.

THE TWO NUMBERS AGREE: Tree.from(page) on this module's own subtree rendered 9 rows - compare, keys, words, Drag, Overview, Overview/intro, Docs, doc/decisions, Files - every one an <a> with a real url, against 9 pages counted by walking page.children recursively. Deeper levels are a function on the node, so they fetch on first open (the same seam core/Page took for data-backed children).

LAYOUT FINDING, fixed: the first build put the tree in a .rail beside a pane. Inside a Doc's detail column the stage is 556px wide and the rail measured 168px, so a row carrying a grip, a caret, an icon, a star, a + and a x had about 30px left for its label - every row read 'S...'. The tree now takes the full width of the demo with the readouts under it (556px), and the tree box scrolls at 24em because 'Open every branch' is 3,700px of rows. Also found and fixed in the template: .ui-tree-text had overflow:hidden + ellipsis but no min-width:0, so a long label pushed the row wider instead of truncating - which is what pushed the new buttons off the end.

TWO LATENT BUGS FOUND BY READING, both fixed in the merge. (1) TreeKeys.moves() read [...rows.values()] and its own comment claimed that was DOM order - true only while every row was built depth-first and synchronously. A lazily-loaded branch sets its rows on the Map long after its neighbours, so the arrows would have walked out of order the moment children could arrive late; moves() now reads the DOM and maps back through a by_el Map. (2) TreeDrag's locate_parent() tested `n.children &&` - a function is truthy, so an unopened lazy branch would have thrown inside the recursion on the first drop; it tests is.arr now.

The `decision` verb LANDED while this task ran - JSONL.js now has decision() and verdict() handlers, not just the verb names. The decision below is written as a decision line; the earlier log line saying the handler was missing was true at 23:25 and is not any more.

decision.about: Three trees exist. Which one becomes the merged tree, and where does it live?

options.say: ux/Tree is the base; lift Make's edge model into it
options.why: Already a real class with parts as statics, already wears ui/tree's markup, already reachable from framework/. It is missing one thing - the drag model - and that is 60 lines.

options.say: Make's tree is the base; move it into ux/
options.why: It has the better drag (three targets, measured) and the row acts. But its rows carry a PATH into made.js, its drop commits through page.move_to(), it has NO expand and collapse at all, and it lives in /imagine/ where nothing in framework/ may import it - so the move means deleting its writer half and adding folding, the keyboard and a nodes-array source.

options.say: A new tree under ui/ that all three adopt
options.why: A clean sheet, and a fourth tree on the site until the other three are retired - which is the problem this task exists to fix.

decision.because: The merge is additive there: one class keeps its whole public API, gains Make's one good idea, and is the only one of the three a page in framework/ can import.
decision.note: ui/tree stays the markup and CSS it wears. Make's tree becomes a consumer in a later task (out of this fence), where it loses roughly 200 of its 343 lines.

decision.about: Keyboard, drag, drill-down and row buttons - subclasses, or properties on one class?

options.say: One class; drag / adapt / acts are properties, keyboard always on
options.why: A consumer can have all four at once. The module's own doctrine (your case is a subclass, never an option) was written before anyone wanted two of them together.

options.say: Keep TreeKeys and TreeDrag as subclasses and add TreeAdapt beside them
options.why: Follows the module's stated doctrine - and reproduces the exact defect: they are siblings, JavaScript has single inheritance, so no tree can have two.

options.say: Compose the three as mixin functions over Tree
options.why: Gives every combination, and adds a pattern this codebase does not use anywhere else.

decision.because: The sibling-subclass shape is what made the page CMS write a third tree, and that is a measured cost rather than a taste.
decision.note: TreeKeys.js and TreeDrag.js stay as back-compat shims, so every documented call still works; TreeDrag keeps its moved(node, into, at) spelling on top of the new move({node, into, index}).

decision.about: The owner's 'each selection changes the visibility of siblings and how deep' - what exactly folds?

options.say: Shut everything, re-open the chain from the root to the selected row, the row included
options.why: You see your ancestors, every level's siblings as shut rows you can still click, and your own children. Four lines, and sideways navigation is never taken away.

options.say: HIDE the siblings of ancestors rather than shutting them
options.why: Fewer rows still - but you can no longer move sideways at any level above you without going back up, so the tree stops being navigable.

options.say: Keep a fixed window of N levels around the selection
options.why: A number to tune, and it hides ancestors, which is the one thing a drill-down must keep.

decision.because: It is the smallest rule that answers the sentence, and it leaves every row that is folded still on screen and still clickable.
decision.note: Measured on the module page's five-level tree: 138 rows with every branch open, 12 at depth four with adapt on. Off by default, and one property to change, because the owner said getting it right takes practice.

log.msg: PUBLIC API PROVEN INTACT, live in the browser (import of all three modules, constructed with capture:false). TreeKeys: 4 rows, exactly ONE tabbable row (the roving tabindex), moves() = 4, onSelect fired, root still wears ux-tree-keys. TreeDrag: root wears ux-tree-drag, 4 grips drawn, onMoved(node, into, at) fired ['c','d',0] from the new move() event. Plain Tree: 0 grips, drag off by default. draw, select, focus_row, expand, moved, Tree.Item and Tree.Row are all still functions. Nothing outside ux/Tree imported these anyway - rg 'ux/Tree' over public --glob '*.js' returns only prose mentions and the module's own pages - so the shims are for the documented API, not for a caller.

CRAWL: /framework/ux/Tree/ and its four children, plus /framework/ui/tree/ and /framework/ux/, at 400 / 1280 / 1920. Zero console errors at every width, zero horizontal overflow at every width, and zero clipped .ui-tree-text (measured as scrollWidth > clientWidth + 1, not by looking for an ellipsis character). At 400 the two readout panes stack, which needed a 15em min-width floor: .flex-1 is flex 1 1 0 with no basis, so without it they split a 280px phone stage into two 130px columns.

LEFT, with reasons. (1) Make's tree is still its own 343 lines - it is read-only in this brief, and converting it is its own task with its own drag re-proof. (2) No ARIA roles (role=tree, aria-expanded): unchanged from 2026-08-21 and now worth more, because with the keyboard in the base class every tree on the site would gain them at once - a real design pass, not three attributes. (3) core/Sidebar keeps its flat list; a tree would add nesting nothing asks for (proposal only, and it is outside the fence). (4) draw() still resets what is open, and the caller still writes it back in one line - the module page shows that line rather than hiding it; worth a seam only if a third consumer writes it.

assign.outcome:
**One tree.** There were three, and none of them could do the job: `ux/Tree` shipped the keyboard and the drag as *sibling* subclasses, so no tree could have both — which is why the page CMS wrote its own, with no expand and collapse at all. They are one class now, and everything else is a switch.

```js
new Tree({ nodes, drag: true, adapt: true, acts: "default add remove" })
Tree.from(page)   // a page's children, as a tree of real links
```

**A row is three drop targets** — top edge *above*, middle *inside*, bottom edge *below* — Make's model, lifted whole, and all three arrive as one event, `move({ node, into, index })`. The tree never writes.

![above](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/tree-component/shots/drag-above.png)
![inside](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/tree-component/shots/drag-inside.png)
![below](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/tree-component/shots/drag-below.png)

**`adapt: true` — the drill-down.** Selecting a row shuts everything and re-opens just the chain you are on, the row included, so you see your ancestors, your siblings at every level and your own children. On the module page's five-level tree: **138 rows fully open, 12 at depth four.**

![adapt at depth four](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/tree-component/shots/adapt-depth-4.png)

**Left:** Make's tree is still its own 343 lines (read-only in this brief; converting it is its own task, worth ~200 lines back). No ARIA roles — unchanged since 2026-08-21, and now worth more, because every tree would gain them at once. `core/Sidebar` keeps its flat list; a tree would add nesting nothing asks for.
